state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. In this case, the student needs to understand that changing all values by the same proportion will affect the range.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get that changing all the values by the same proportion does affect the range. But I'm still not sure how it works with the examples. Can you explain why cutting the heights in half and adding \(3 \mathrm{~cm}\) each would change the range differently?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. In this case, cutting the heights in half and adding \(3 \mathrm{~cm}\) each are different operations that will change the range in different ways.
